evidence.text: Choose a charge normal form, differentiate a linear combination of its magnitudes, and match all quadratic terms to the known charge potential. Quotient equivalent coefficient choices and retain those with the required horizon critical point.

sources.title: Moduli stabilization, large-volume dS minimum without D3-bar branes, (non-)supersymmetric black hole attractors and two-parameter Swiss cheese Calabi-Yau's

evidence.text: Complex-structure stabilization solves covariant superpotential equations, including τ=(fᵀΠ̄)/(hᵀΠ̄). Kähler stabilization uses the N=1 scalar potential with perturbative and nonperturbative α′ corrections and theta-function-dressed Euclidean D3 instanton contributions.

sources.title: First Order Description of D=4 static Black Holes and the Hamilton-Jacobi equation

evidence.text: Standard Hamilton–Jacobi canonical transformations generate first-order equations through pi=∂iW and q̇i=Gij∂jW. Constant new momenta encode integration constants; the original energy constraint supplies the Hamilton–Jacobi equation.

sources.title: Fake Superpotential for Large and Small Extremal Black Holes

evidence.text: Reviewed Hamilton–Jacobi formulation: characteristic function S=2e^U W, with W²+2G^{rs}∂rW∂sW=V. The radial equations are U̇=e^U W and φ̇^r=2e^U G^{rs}∂sW. For the chosen solution class, W(φ0,P)=∫_{−∞}^0 e^{2U}V dτ=M_ADM; Appendix A derives the flow by varying boundary data.

sources.title: Black holes in supergravity: flow equations and duality

evidence.text: Radial reduction and elimination of electric potentials give a one-dimensional mechanical action with V_BH = −QᵀMQ/2. A separate Hamiltonian constraint is essential for equivalence to the original field equations.

sources.title: Moduli, scalar charges, and the first law of black hole thermodynamics

evidence.text: Reduce the static spherical field equations to radial equations for U and φ^a with potential V and an energy constraint. Differentiate V twice along the radial solution and integrate a nonnegative expression to constrain zero-scalar-charge solutions.

sources.title: Universality of supersymmetric attractors

evidence.text: Does central-charge extremization determine supersymmetric black-hole horizon area universally when extended supersymmetry supplies several central-charge eigenvalues?

sources.title: Covariant formulation of BPS black holes and the scalar weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can central-charge geometry and covariant BPS black-hole equations support a scalar weak-gravity relation involving mass, first derivatives and second derivatives in extended supergravity?

sources.title: First order description of black holes in moduli space

evidence.text: Does a real function of the moduli generate non-BPS extremal black-hole evolution and its attractor endpoints? The paper also asks how far such a description can survive when the non-extremality parameter is nonzero.

sources.title: (Un)attractor black holes in higher derivative AdS gravity

evidence.text: How do Gauss–Bonnet corrections affect renormalized charges, thermodynamics and scalar attractor behavior of static charged AdS black holes, including extremal solutions?

sources.title: Moduli flow and non-supersymmetric AdS attractors

evidence.text: Do static, non-supersymmetric extremal AdS black holes exhibit moduli attraction with scalar-coupled higher-curvature terms, and can the radial moduli flow be interpreted holographically as an RG flow with a monotonic c-function?

sources.title: Supersymmetry and attractors

evidence.text: Can the horizon area and entropy of supersymmetric extremal black holes be obtained by extremizing the central charge over moduli, explaining their independence from asymptotic scalar values?

sources.title: Flow Equations for Non-BPS Extremal Black Holes

evidence.text: Under what conditions can non-BPS extremal black holes obey first-order radial flow equations driven by a fake superpotential, and how can such generators be constructed using the analogy with domain walls?

sources.title: Freezing of moduli by N=2 dyons

evidence.text: Construct supersymmetric black holes whose vector and hypermultiplet scalars remain constant from horizon to infinity, and determine how electric and magnetic charges fix the vector moduli.

sources.title: Flows of extremal attractor black holes

evidence.text: How do nonsupersymmetric extremal AdS attractor black holes change after adding a dilaton bare potential representing a relevant deformation, and which resulting branches are thermodynamically preferred?

sources.title: Fake supersymmetry versus Hamilton-Jacobi

evidence.text: When do Hamilton–Jacobi first-order flows reduce to standard fake-superpotential flows, and what does this distinction imply for regular extremal black holes and small-hole near-horizon scalar motion?

sources.title: Black holes as probes of moduli space geometry

evidence.text: Can measurements in one vacuum probe the geometry and effective couplings of faraway moduli-space regions using finite-energy BPS black holes, and how do accessible distance and resolution depend on available mass and charge?

sources.title: Some comments on gravitational entropy and the inverse mean curvature flow

evidence.text: Can inverse mean curvature flow extend mass and horizon-area bounds to asymptotically AdS black holes with nontrivial topology and to gravity with scalar/vector matter, thereby extending charge-dependent attractor bounds beyond static spherical solutions?

sources.title: Noncommutative brane-world, (Anti) de Sitter vacua and extra dimensions

evidence.text: Can a curved brane-world inspired by a noncommutative D3-brane support static dS/AdS black holes with different horizon topologies, and can its extremal limits explain attractor behavior and suggest extra dimensions?

sources.title: Black Holes, Moduli Stabilisation and the Swampland

evidence.text: How does cosmological moduli stabilisation change scalar excursions near charged extremal black holes, and what implications follow for horizon-scale UV physics and the consistency of rigid compactifications?

destination.summary: A comparative overview of distinct SYK constructions. Reparametrization soft modes, charge projection and long-range scrambling are separate mechanisms; maximal chaos and approximate conformality do not transfer automatically between them.

Interacting complex SYK with gauged U(1) and a charge-k Wilson line
Two-dimensional long-range bosonic SYK
Boundary Yukawa-SYK for the reported hyperbolic-chaos observable

sources.title: Remarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model

evidence.text: Sum leading large-N diagrams through Schwinger–Dyson equations G(ω)^−1=−iω−Σ(ω), Σ(τ)=J²G(τ)^(q−1). A disorder-averaged bilocal functional integral supplies the saddle action and fluctuation expansion.

sources.title: Gauging the complex SYK model

evidence.text: Gaussian disorder averaging introduces bilocal G and Sigma. Their large-N saddle equations are solved by iterative Fourier methods, supplemented by conformal ansätze and an analytic large-q expansion.

sources.title: Remarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model

evidence.text: Extract chaos using a retarded ladder kernel and the ansatz F(t1,t2)=exp[λL(t1+t2)/2]f(t12), requiring kernel eigenvalue one. Numerical real-time Schwinger–Dyson iteration and binary search implement this condition at finite coupling.

sources.title: Remarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model

evidence.text: Sum connected ladders as F=(1−K)^−1F0. In the conformal limit, diagonalize K using the SL(2) Casimir, hypergeometric eigenfunctions, and contour deformation; the complete spectral basis includes h=1/2+is and h=2,4,6,… .

sources.title: Gauging the complex SYK model

evidence.text: Expand the bilocal action to quadratic order; solve the conformal ladder-kernel eigenvalue-one condition for background-field dimensions. Analytically continue to a retarded kernel and study late-time OTOC double commutators for chaos.

sources.title: Gauging the complex SYK model

evidence.text: Compute holonomy integrals either through polynomial fits and Gaussian/Hermite integration or through complex saddles on the imaginary-u axis. The latter implements the grand-canonical to canonical Legendre transform. Compare both approaches with disorder-averaged exact diagonalization.

destination.question: Which operator spectra and correlators can be computed or constrained using melonic, large-charge, flavor-ratio and boundary-bulk constructions, and which reality or symmetry protections hold in each?
destination.summary: These constructions share a target of accessible conformal data, not a common expansion. The nonsupersymmetric melonic model, finite-rank supersymmetric theory, bifundamental gauge theory and boundary model retain separate fine identities.

systems: Three-dimensional disordered Gross–Neveu–Yukawa theory
Finite-rank N=4 SYM, principally SU(2) for the non-BPS large-charge spectrum
Nonsupersymmetric U(N) × U(M) Chern–Simons theory with bifundamental fermions
Long-range bosonic SYK and three-dimensional boundary Yukawa-SYK coupled to a four-dimensional free bulk
targets: Reality of single-trace dimensions
Non-BPS spectra, structure constants and HHLL correlators
Strong-coupling anomalous dimensions beginning with tr(ψ̄ψ)
Boundary operator protection and central-charge data
regimes: Large M,N at fixed M/N for the disordered GNY model
J → ∞ with λJ = gYM²J/2 fixed at finite rank
First order in M/N at λN = 0, to all orders in λM, for the stated Chern–Simons calculation
The boundary point Δϕ = 1 for the protected higher-spin displacement tower
assumptions: Reality of the calculated single-trace spectrum is not a complete stability theorem
General SU(N) localization results concern integrated HHLL correlators; they do not establish the full SU(2) spectral result at every rank
The M/N expansion does not establish solvability of the full equal-rank matrix model
conventions: Dirac and Majorana GNY spectra have different operator content
Flavor-ratio, large-charge and melonic expansions are distinguished
includes: Ordinary field-theory calculations with conjectural gravitational applications
excludes: Universal higher-spin protection across the models

sources.title: Anomalous dimensions in non-supersymmetric bifundamental Chern-Simons theories

evidence.text: The anomalous dimension is extracted from logarithmic divergences of the scalar two-point function. Integrals use Feynman parameters and a hard momentum cutoff Λ in the Euclidean 1–2 plane.

sources.title: Spectrum of a Gross-Neveu Yukawa model with flavor disorder in three dimensions

evidence.text: Uses conformally invariant three-point structures and melonic ladder kernels, selecting dimensions where a kernel eigenvalue equals one. Generic positive-spin parity-even/odd kernels are 3×3/2×2; corresponding scalar kernels are 2×2/1×1, with further reductions for odd spin.

sources.title: Large charge ’t Hooft limit of $ \mathcal{N} $ = 4 super-Yang-Mills

evidence.text: Perturbative dilatation-operator diagonalization in scalar and derivative subsectors; contour projection of free partition functions and the superconformal index tests the constrained-magnon counting.

sources.title: Anomalous dimensions in non-supersymmetric bifundamental Chern-Simons theories

evidence.text: An infinite chain of gauge-field self-energy insertions is resummed as G = (1 − DΣ)^−1D. The scalar two-point calculation includes fermion self-energy, vertex and additional two-point diagrams built with the corrected gauge propagator.

sources.title: Anomalous dimensions in non-supersymmetric bifundamental Chern-Simons theories

evidence.text: The M/N expansion retains genus-zero Feynman diagrams. Small α selects a summable vector-model-like subset; increasing α order enlarges that subset. This differs from a full 1/N expansion because nonplanar diagrams remain excluded.

targets: Local two-dimensional Poincaré algebra
Maximal modular growth

conventions: Modular evolution is distinguished from ordinary thermal time evolution

includes: Horizon motivation and nongravitational algebraic realizations
